The AT-2855 negative control (explicit alpha=0.0 SUPPLIED, not omitted) correctly bypasses the new preflight check and reaches real dispatch, producing the vacuous PASS that proves the guard's necessity -- this is the right way to test a guard against its own absence.

CRIT-2's reframe is intellectually honest and the mechanism is sound: 'structurally defeats' is now scoped correctly to the source-annotation channel (true: @equiv_fp_tol has no HIR lowering, verified in r1), and the MCP request-level knob is explicitly named 'governed, not eliminated' with a concrete mechanism (server-owned default via default_bit_exact + tolerance_overridden stamp + notes entry). CRIT-3's [-1,1] well-conditioned float-fill formula is not just plausible, it matches an ALREADY-ESTABLISHED codebase pattern: crates/axc-driver/src/q4km_oracle.rs, q5k_oracle.rs, q6k_oracle.rs all use half::f16::from_f32(v).to_bits() with v in comparable bounded ranges (e.g. q4km_oracle.rs:461 `(((i*7+3)%100) as f32)/100.0 - 0.5`, q5k_oracle.rs:396 `/50.0 - 1.0`) for exactly the same purpose (finite, payload-stable f16 test data for Q4_K_M-family kernels). The r2 fill formula (`rng_b.next_u32()` normalized to [-1,1], stored via the same half::f16::from_f32 path) is a seeded generalization of a pattern this codebase already trusts for f16 buffers -- not a novel, unverified idea. Verified by direct source read, not grep-only.

WARN-1's fix creates a clean, gap-free partition rather than a patch with a seam: mandatory-explicit-workgroups fires exactly when `coopmat.is_some() || shared_memory_bytes>0`, and the (already-existing, optimistic-minor-folded) `--size` shortcut is restricted to exactly the complementary set (`coopmat.is_none() && shared_memory_bytes==0`). Every kernel class is covered by exactly one rule; there is no kernel shape that falls through both (i.e., that needs mandatory workgroups AND is eligible for the underspecified derive path).

WARN-2's determinism self-check is placed correctly in the pipeline (§3.1 step 7, before the rewritten dispatch, after GPU-availability) and its output feeds the differential compare correctly ('the first original run' vs rewritten, step 9) -- the two original dispatches are not wasted, the first one is reused as the actual oracle for the real comparison, so the self-check costs exactly one extra dispatch as claimed, not two extra.

WARN-3's closed verdict/stage/reason.kind tables in §5 are now genuinely exhaustive and every AT in §8 references a reason.kind that exists in that table (workgroups_required, push_constants_required, preflight_fail_rewritten, preflight_fail_original, original_nondeterministic, gpu_unavailable, coopmat_unsupported, numeric_mismatch, interface_mismatch -- all cross-checked present, no AT references an undefined kind).

The saxpy_reassoc.axc fixture (WARN-5) is a genuine single-commutation, not a re-association, and the spec is precise about this: original computes `alpha*x[i] + y[i]`, rewritten computes `y[i] + alpha*x[i]` -- both are `add(A, B)` on the SAME two operands (the scalar product and y[i]), just argument-order-swapped at the single top-level add. IEEE-754 754-2019 §5.4.1 defines addition as producing the correctly-rounded result of the exact sum of the operand VALUES (an unordered pair); round-to-nearest-even is symmetric under operand swap, so a+b and b+a round identically for all finite, non-NaN operands -- this is a true bit-exact guarantee, distinct from re-association (e.g. (a+b)+c vs a+(b+c)) which is NOT generally bit-exact and which this fixture correctly does not attempt. The well-conditioned [-1,1] fill (CRIT-3) guarantees non-NaN operands, closing the one edge case (NaN quieting/payload) where even commutativity can look order-dependent at the bit level.
